results.content: In phase 1, 1294 rectal and vaginal swabs were collected from pregnant women and inoculated in enrichment (Lim) broth, which was then tested using the HG GBS LAMP assay (*sip* gene target) and culture on chromogenic agar. This is the first study to investigate rapid diagnostic tests in labor for the assessment of GBS rectovaginal colonization in Uganda and the first to indicate acceptable sensitivity and specificity of the HG GBS LAMP assay, compared to culture, regardless of a pre-enrichment step. For direct swab testing, similar sensitivity results were reported in a prior study evaluating diagnostic accuracy the HG GBS LAMP assay in Ireland (92.2%) [14], as well as other studies evaluating rapid molecular-based assays, including the GeneOhm IDI-strep B (91.1%) [17] and quantitative PCR (95.5%) [18].
